title: Attention prefetch+fusion latency postmortem
content:
Summary:

This is a working postmortem for the regression that surfaced 2025-11-05 where tail latency for small, bursty chat workloads increased ~3x on a mix of FlashAttention + paged-attention paths when fused ops were enabled. The hypothesis space is focused on prefetching heuristics interacting with kernel fusion selection—particularly the path that switches between flashpaged and fused kernels under mid-sequence-length tails.

Context / What we saw:
- Symptom: p95/p99 token completion latency rose from baseline (~45ms) to ~150ms on a particular customer workload (many short prompts with a few long continuations).
- Affected stack: serving runtime 1.14, kernel chooser v2, fusion opt-in enabled via config flag fusedops=true.
- Reproducible in lab with micro-workloads that mix seq_len=32 and seq_len=1024 in the same connection.
- Non-affected: pure long sequences (all seq>512) and pure short sequences (all seq<64) appear normal.

Investigations performed (chronological):
1) Canary reproducer:
   - Wrote small harness that issues bursts of 16 concurrent requests: 12 at seq_len=32 (prompt) followed by 4 at seq_len=1024 (continuation).
   - Observed p99 latency spikes only when the burst interleaves long and short sequences in same process.

2) Telemetry correlation:
   - Traced kernel selection log for each request. Found patterns where the runtime switches between flashpaged kernel and fused-kernel mid-batch due to batching heuristics and per-request seq distribution.
   - KV-cache prefetch counters showed elevated prefetch aborts (prefetch started then cancelled) in the fusion path.

3) Microbenchmarks:
   - Isolated kernels (no batching): flashattn (FA) vs paged-attn (PA) vs fused-attn-op (FO) measured on GPU A100.
   - Single-call latency: FO ~ FA for long sequences, FO slightly worse ~8% for seq_len=32.
   - Small-batch (batch=4) mixed seq: When FO was chosen mid-batch the per-token overhead increased (kernel launch jitter + extra mem copies).

4) Kernel handshake and warmup profiling:
   - Captured CUDA event latencies surrounding kernel launches. Noted extra gaps when FO and FA were interleaved. Handshake cost equals additional 20–60us per switch, but accumulated across tokens and batched micro-scheduling becomes visible at p99.

5) Paging & prefetch traces:
   - Paged-attn path does on-demand page bringing of KV shards. FA path uses contiguous memory access and benefits from aggressive prefetch of next KV slab.
   - When fusion chooses to combine ops, the prefetch plan changes; we see cases where PA prefetch is scheduled, then FO runs which expects contiguous KV and ends up issuing a small number of synchronous device copies. That pattern stalls the scheduler and produces a microburst.

Key hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Heuristic thrash between prefetch strategies. When kernel chooser oscillates, the prefetch planner starts work for one strategy then cancels or overlaps with the alternate strategy causing device-side contention and blocking copies. (High likelihood)
- H2: Batching coalescer incorrectly groups mixed-seq requests in a way that triggers suboptimal kernel layout requiring extra workspace allocations and memcpy. (Medium)
- H3: Kernel ABI differences cause additional register pressure and occasional kernel relaunch with different workspace size—leading to page faults for paged-attn on the same stream. (Lower but possible for some models)

Evidence supporting H1:
- Prefetch abort counter correlates tightly with latency spikes (r > 0.87).
- Reproducer where we disable kernel-chooser (force FA or force FO) removes spikes.
- Synthetic pattern that flips selection every request increases spike frequency.

Immediate mitigation options tested in lab:
- Option A: Disable fusedops for mixed-length workloads via route-level config (works but loses FO perf on long sequences).
- Option B: Add hysteresis to kernel chooser so it prefers the current kernel unless there's sustained evidence to switch (reduced spikes by ~70%).
- Option C: Make prefetch planner use a token-granular cancellation fence instead of synchronous memcpy cancelation (experimental, reduced aborts but introduced new ordering complexity).

Short-term recommendation (<= 2 weeks):
- Rollback: Toggle fusedops=false for affected customers only (safety).
- Deploy heuristic patch: kernel chooser hysteresis (small change, low risk) on canary fleet to validate reduction in tail spikes.
- Add runtime flag to make prefetch planner conservative when batch has mixed seq lengths (diagnostic only).

Longer-term work (owner suggestions):
- Preload model of expected per-connection length distribution via ingestion of historical traffic. Use this to bias prefetch strategy per-connection (Priya).
- Rework prefetch cancellation: make it non-blocking and overlap with scheduling token generation (Marcus).
- Improve batching coalescer to respect kernel-affinity tags (Jordan).
- Add microbenchmark harness that simulates mixed-seq conversational workloads and runs nightly (Ava / SRE).

Experiment notes and commands (lab):
- reproducer: tools/bench/mixed_seq_repro --concurrency 16 --pattern 12x32+4x1024 --runtime 1.14 --fusedops on/off
- trace capture: runtime/bin/trace_dump --pid $PID --filter "kernel_choice|prefetch" > trace.log
- kernel-level benchmark: tools/gpu-kernel-bench --kernel flashattn --seq 1024 --batch 4 --iter 500

Raw micro-results (median of 5 runs):
- baseline (fusedops=false): p50=40ms p95=62ms p99=78ms
- fusedops=true, no hysteresis: p50=43ms p95=120ms p99=148ms
- fusedops=true + chooser-hysteresis: p50=42ms p95=68ms p99=86ms

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm if similar pattern exists on other GPU types (H100/RTX6000) — Marcus to run this week.
- [ ] Check whether custom quantized kernels change memory layout effects causing extra memcopies.
- [ ] Validate that disabling prefetch for mixed-batches doesn't regress throughput significantly for long-running streams.

Notes for follow-up postmortem doc (final):
- Capture customer impact summary and exact routes affected.
- Time-ordered changelog of commits in kernel chooser and prefetch planner for last 3 releases.
- Performance delta matrix (GPU x model x seq-mix) to guide rollout scaffolding.

Appendix: Observability artifacts captured
- trace.log excerpts (attached to JIRA SRV-1427)
- perf flamegraphs: s3://redwood-bench/attn/2025-11-07/mixedseq-flame.svg
- kernel selection scatter: confluence.redwood/attn-kernel-scatter-2025-11-07

Meeting notes (11-11-2025):
- Decision: do not globally rollback fusedops. Proceed with canary for hysteresis and route-level fusedops opt-out for high-risk customers.
- Action items assigned above; follow-up sync on 11-18-2025.

Notes-to-self: Keep this doc informal. Move to final postmortem after final rollout and metrics stabilize (p99 within 2x baseline).

References and links:
- GH PR 2198 (kernel chooser refactor)
- Confluence design: Attn prefetch planner v3

notes_summary: Working postmortem tracing latency regression to prefetch+fusion heuristic thrash. Short-term: hysteresis and route opt-out. Long-term: prefetch redesign and batching coalescer affinity.
